goal: Use a playable approximate roles AI through the existing battle lab, Player/API and evaluation/replay commands: infer useful opponent responses from the known deck and current board, preserve strategically different response types, search enabling sequences, and never read actual hidden information.
persona: Developer/player using the existing local battle lab to inspect AI decisions and replay complete registered-deck matches on Windows.
public_entry: http://127.0.0.1:8767/ battle lab; POST /api/ai-step; public Player interface; .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 -m svdeck.battle_training evaluate/replay and svdeck.battle replay. T3 uses the dedicated documented storage-isolated session at http://127.0.0.1:8767/?session=1a0b51fd-208e-4ac1-af72-eed792b6f97e on that same battle-lab server.
test_data: docs/evidence/role-response/independent-fixtures.v1.json is the frozen independent oracle and fixture recipe.
Registered ramp-dragon and last-words-nightmare 40-card snapshots from src/svdeck/data/battle_decks.json; no current-meta lookup.

roles is the new policy name. Use documented K configuration with values 3,5,10. Executor may write an adapter using public interfaces; neither expected results nor fixture values may be changed to fit output.
minimal_test_count_rationale: Three independent journeys cover three distinct entry contracts: tactical/model correctness, complete headless play/replay, and the human selector/save/reopen flow. Small probes are grouped in one journey to avoid redundant setup; the two full games cover roles in both seats without pretending to estimate strength.

tests.title: Fixed tactical cases and response coverage across K
tests.user_task: Determine whether the new AI finds sensible tactical responses, respects effect conditions and hand availability, and explains what its finite search covered.
setup: Fresh isolated Python process/output directory; only public docs, frozen fixture oracle and public entry contracts are provided to the executor.

Expand common_cards/state_defaults in the frozen fixture without changing values. Use synthetic Battle fixtures for small probes and the supplied real-card metadata semantics. Keep RNG/config fixed across K apart from K itself.

The documented diagnostic interface must expose response traces, required-card multisets, role goals and search coverage. Missing product diagnostics needed to inspect a promised behavior are a product finding, not an independence excuse.
actions: Run F1-F5 and the two metadata checks once per K=3,5,10 through Player and the documented response diagnostic entry; record per-call wall time/process peak memory, depth, candidate counts, role coverage and limits.

Replay the selected actions and candidate witness sequences through the normal public Battle engine; compare against frozen independent effects and arithmetic. Enumerate the three F3 hands directly for overlap arithmetic without importing policy helpers.

Run the hidden-information metamorphic pair once at K=5 through Player and /api/ai-step, fixing role seed; compare the visible inputs and semantic decisions before any real action advances hidden state.
functional_expectations: F1 and F2 choose and legally execute the fixed sensible action. F3 retains healing/single removal, defense/development and area removal responses for every K, with the stated distinct outcomes and feasible PP/hand multiplicity.

F3 marginal and joint availability agree with the three-hand oracle under its stated uniform model; overlapping hands and a multi-role physical card are not counted twice as disjoint mass. A response requiring three cards has zero availability when hand size is two.
F4 includes the generation enabler then generated damage in that order; availability depends on maker, not a nonexistent original burn card. F5 does not claim an inactive conditional effect.
Metadata for the two registered cards retains multiple roles, timing, target selection/count, and activation conditions. Exact field names may differ if public semantics are clear.

Hidden hand/deck/RNG mutations leave public observations and semantic choices equal. Ordinary roles judgments clearly identify approximate opponent modeling, never inferred opponent hands as actual knowledge, and never call hypothetical response modeling a guaranteed optimum/win rate.

K comparison reports actual correctness, coverage, time, memory, requested/completed depth and stopping reason. A larger K is not required to win more games or be faster. Existing policies remain selectable/accepted.
ux_checks: This headless journey has no browser interaction requirement. A reader can identify the chosen action, assumed response types, approximate nature and any cutoff in the public judgment/report without reading implementation source.
Time is measured from public decision-call entry until return using a monotonic clock; memory reports method and scope. These are observations, not an invented pass/fail latency threshold.
impossible_if: The machine cannot execute the installed Python runtime after safe environment repair, or required registered card data is unavailable. A wrong decision, crash, missing roles option, missing diagnostics, or ordinary search cutoff is a product result, not execution impossibility.
tests.isolation_requirements: Dedicated process and output directory; do not inspect product source/diff, existing candidate output or implementer explanations. Executor may inspect public docs and actual public results only after the spec is locked.

budget.basis: One scripted batch of five small probes across three K values, two metadata checks, candidate replay and one metamorphic pair; no broad benchmark or repeats.

tests.title: Registered-deck games and saved replay in both seats
tests.user_task: Run two complete deck-vs-deck games with roles controlling both seat positions across the pair, and use their saved replays to verify the games.
setup: Separate process/output directory, registered 40-card snapshots, fixed seed 93001, roles versus existing search policy using the frozen full_game_pair.

Use documented finite defaults; record exact command/options and versions. If evaluate schedules extra matchup permutations, use its public selection options or public play API for precisely the frozen pair, and exercise evaluate once as a bounded integration check.
actions: Invoke existing evaluation/replay interfaces with the new roles name; run the frozen pair to a real terminal result, save per-game decision and measurement records.

Validate every recorded action as legal at its execution point and load each export through the existing replay command/API, comparing final winner, leaders, boards, hands/decks and saved decision identity.
Read the comparison report and verify it distinguishes game outcome counts, unfinished games, actual search depth and resource measurements.
functional_expectations: Both frozen games terminate without illegal action, crash or synthetic turn-limit win; roles is exercised as seat0 and seat1. A budget stop is recorded as unfinished and is not called a complete game.
Both complete records replay to the exact saved final state and preserve new policy judgments. evaluate/replay accept roles; existing search remains usable.

Report time, peak memory and measurement scope, completed depth/cutoffs and candidate coverage for the pair. Two results are demonstrations of playable/legal execution, not statistical evidence of superior strength or a claimed win rate guarantee.
ux_checks: Headless results identify deck names, roles seat, policy names, terminal outcome or incomplete status, replay locations and resource measurements in a concise readable report; no source inspection needed.
No UI clicks or focus transitions apply. Measure total CLI elapsed time from process launch to exit with a monotonic clock, separately from individual decision times.
impossible_if: Registered 40-card snapshots or the installed runtime are missing/unreadable after safe environment repair; missing new policy integration, replay disagreement or unfinished play is a product result.
tests.isolation_requirements: Independent process/output directory from T1/T3. Do not alter shared saved battle-lab state. Use only public entry points and frozen data.

budget.basis: Two registered-deck games, a bounded evaluation entry check, and two replay validations. This is an observation budget, not a per-decision SLA or a basis to call unfinished games complete.

tests.title: Select roles, execute a step, save and reopen its judgment
tests.user_task: Use the new AI in the usual battle lab and inspect the saved explanation of its move.
setup: Dedicated browser tab at http://127.0.0.1:8767/?session=1a0b51fd-208e-4ac1-af72-eed792b6f97e, Windows desktop viewport 1366x768, fresh isolated session storage as documented in docs/battle-roles.md, no login required, no unrelated tabs/windows touched. This UUID is newly allocated only for T3; do not open it for preliminary probes or other work. Its saved battle, replay position, starting condition, hand display, AI choice and animation preference start from the documented empty/default state and remain separate from the normal URL and other sessions.
Start the existing ramp-dragon versus last-words-nightmare condition in that tab; turn animation off using the existing control. Use the new roles selector entry; start with no saved replay loaded.
actions: Find roles in the existing AI selector and choose it, then execute one AI step using the existing button; directly log clicks/keys/scrolls, active tab, selected option and observed start/end times.
Inspect the resulting board and judgment in the battle-lab tab, save the record using the existing save control, reopen it through the existing open control and navigate to the saved step.
Confirm the saved roles choice/judgment matches the executed step and that existing policies remain in the selector.
functional_expectations: The selected roles policy reaches /api/ai-step, produces one legal state transition and a saved roles judgment. The new option has a human-readable label that conveys opponent response/role reasoning.

The reopened record reproduces the step and its judgment. Approximate assumptions/limits are understandable, and hypothetical hand estimates are not presented as revealed actual cards or guaranteed optimal play.
ux_checks: At 1366x768 after choosing a registered starting condition, the existing AI selector, execute-one-step control and board are visible/enabled without page scrolling; inspect through live DOM/accessibility plus screenshot. Diagnostic details may remain in the existing details panel.

From selecting roles through observing the first result, remain in the same battle-lab tab with selected policy roles; no unsolicited new window/tab or manual window switch is required. Do not steal focus into another surface. Record the actual clicks, scrolls and elapsed time directly; no arbitrary total-click or latency ceiling is imposed.

Save/open may invoke the normal file chooser and replay navigation. The chosen policy and result must remain legible without clipping at 1366x768. Do not infer intermediate interaction counts or focus changes from the final screenshot.

Judge whether this can ship as-is to the ordinary battle-lab user and name the largest concrete UX issue, or explicitly state none observed. Internal identifiers/diagnostics must not obscure the selected policy, chosen move and visible result; distinguish a thinking/cutoff state from success.
impossible_if: The local server or a controllable browser is unavailable after safe startup/repair. A missing option, broken interaction, clipped new label, AI error or missing saved judgment is a product finding.
tests.isolation_requirements: Dedicated browser tab and isolated session-scoped browser storage on the normal origin; no need to change global browser/app settings or clear any existing data. Keep the same dedicated session URL throughout T3 and keep T2 replay files separate from this UI-created record.

budget.basis: One selector/step flow plus existing save/open and judgment navigation; UI proof is deliberately one representative interaction rather than both full games.

covered_risks: Current lethal and visible defensive trade
Multi-role, conditional and generation-enabler responses with order
Overlap-safe hand availability and finite K coverage
Hidden information isolation and honest approximate diagnostics
Both seat positions in complete legal replayable registered-deck play
blind_spots: Two games and five small cases cannot establish strength, statistical win rates, optimality or complete tactical coverage.
Normal Battle is shared for replay/legality; the finite arithmetic/effect expectations are independent, but this does not independently prove every engine rule.
No latest-meta lookup, all-class deck coverage, human-expert matchup, long training run, mobile UI, or new performance SLA is required.
Memory observations must name process/child-process scope; no claim of exact retained heap size from process peak memory.
